input:
Adsorption of a dye from water on activated carbon was measured in batch tests at 298 K. In a batch test, a fixed mass of adsorbent is contacted with a fixed volume of solution and the concentration is followed as uptake proceeds. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 153 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6. Langmuir capacity is the dye mass taken up per gram of adsorbent at saturation under the Langmuir model, in which uptake rises with concentration and levels off as the surface fills; the fit reports the levelled value, not the uptake at any one concentration.

At an adsorbent dose of 0.7 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 79% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. Adsorbent dose is the adsorbent mass per litre of solution treated, and removal is stated against the initial concentration, so the figure compares the dye removed from solution with the dye present at the start of the test. Each value is tied to its conditions where it is stated: temperature with the tests, pH with the capacity, and dose and contact time with the removal.

The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured, so the capacity and the removal figure describe the dye and carbon pair at the stated pH and temperature. Neither value carries to a different pH, where the charge on the dye and on the carbon surface, and with them the uptake, can differ. The reported removal is a batch-test result at the stated dose; a different dose changes the share of dye removed without changing the capacity the fit returns.
